summary: Tenant concurrency shed-policy interaction causing sustained 5xx wave for high-volume tenant
description:
Issue summary:
A major customer (SkylineDocs, dedicated tier) observed sustained 5xx responses across chat and embedding routes beginning 2026-03-12 12:42 UTC. Error-rate remained elevated for ~90 minutes with periodic recoveries. Impacted flows used the tenant's pinned model variants and high-concurrency streaming sessions.

Impact:
- Customer reported ~40% request failure rate during the window, user-facing timeouts and degraded UX for real-time document Q&A.
- Billing/usage spikes due to hedged retries from client SDKs.
- A few downstream retries triggered CPU/GPU thrash on runtimes, causing additional failures.

Timeline (high level):
- 12:42 UTC: first error spike detected by SkylineDocs alerts (5xx > 15%).
- 12:44 UTC: platform automated alert (apigw 5xx increase) routed to #support and SRE-oncall.
- 12:50–13:10 UTC: intermittent partial recovery correlated with temporary ingress-shed adjustments.
- 13:11 UTC: second spike; overall 5xx floor increased.
- 13:30 UTC: mitigation (route weight shift + tenant cap bump) reduced error rate to <5%.

Environment and scope:
- Region: us-east-1 (single-region Dedicated pool serving SkylineDocs).
- Affected customers: SkylineDocs only (single-tenant observed), but we saw increased backpressure on shared apigw proxies.
- Services: REST generation + streaming chat endpoints, small-batch embedding uploads.

Steps to reproduce (dev notes):
1) Simulate SkylineDocs typical mix: 40% streaming chat (concurrency per-connection 2), 60% short sync generation.
2) Apply tenant concurrency cap = 80 and ingress-thermostat target utilization tuned to 0.85.
3) Ramp traffic to 250 RPS sustained over 5 minutes.
4) Observe apigw 5xx increase and runtime evictions after ~90s when preemptions kick in.

Observed logs / snippets (selected):
- [apigw] 2026-03-12T12:43:01Z ERROR upstream: 502 gateway: conn_reset_by_peer tenant=skyline-docs path=/v1/chat/stream
- [scheduler] 2026-03-12T12:43:05Z WARN preempt: evicting-inflight job job_id=abcd123 reason=tenant_cap_reclaim
- [runtime] 2026-03-12T12:43:07Z ERROR runtime-gpu: preempted due to host-shed (EVIC_TOT) pid=4532 model=open-chat-medium-v2
- [ingress-rate-controller] 2026-03-12T12:43:10Z INFO shed: enqueued 94 requests tenant=skyline-docs policy=thermostat

Metrics observed (links):
- Grafana: apigw/5xx-rate (us-east-1) spike: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ingress/5xx?from=2026-03-12T12:30
- Logs: splunk query id: splunk://query/62a7-skyline-5xx-wave

Investigation notes (SRE):
- Initial hypothesis: standard apigw overload or NVMe iowait (already ruled out by node-level metrics).
- Key finding: when the ingress-thermostat began requeuing because of instantaneous token-bucket depletion, queue depths at the apigw grew and many requests became hedged-retries from the client SDK (SkylineDocs SDK default retries). Hedged retries increased concurrency seen by the scheduler.
- Scheduler responded by reclaiming tenant capacity (tenant concurrency cap enforcement) which triggered inflight preemptions on serving runtimes. Preemptions caused upstream connections to reset and runtimes to emit OOM/preempt errors -> 502/503.
- The interaction path is: influx of hedged retries -> apigw queueing -> ingress-thermostat requeue -> scheduler reclaim -> runtime preempt -> upstream resets -> client retries -> amplification loop.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- 13:30 UTC: increased SkylineDocs tenant concurrency cap from 80 -> 160 (immediate reduction in preemptions).
- 13:32 UTC: adjusted ingress-thermostat to be less aggressive for dedicated-tenants (reduced aggressive requeue threshold).
- 13:35 UTC: shifted a portion of SkylineDocs traffic to a separate warm pool (route weight change).
- Customer applied a short client-side retry-window adjustment per our recommendation.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Primary: Ingress-thermostat requeue behavior interacts poorly with per-tenant concurrency reclamation logic; the system's feedback loop did not account for client hedged-retries and temporarily over-reclaimed capacity leading to preemptive evictions on running GPU workloads.
- Secondary: SkylineDocs client SDK aggressive retry/hedging by default amplified the transient queueing.

Resolution / current status:
- Status: Partial mitigation in place; error-rate returned to acceptable (<5%) but we consider this incident Sev1 until fix deployed.
- Short term: leave tenant cap increased and monitor for 24h. Keep ingress-thermostat relax setting for dedicated pools.
- Long term: scheduled tasks (see Action items) to change reclaim policy and add hedged-retry-awareness to ingress controller.

Action items / follow-ups:
- ENGINEERING-3125: Update scheduler reclaim to prefer draining new capacity before preempting in-flight GPU jobs (owner: Diego Martinez, ETA: 2026-03-19).
- INFRA-2981: Add hedged-retry metric into ingress-thermostat decision loop; avoid requeue when hedged-retry rate > X% (owner: Priya Shah, ETA: 2026-03-18).
- SDK-745: Outreach to SkylineDocs recommending default retry decrease; create opt-in flag for hedging with dedicated customers (owner: DevEx team, ETA: 2026-04-01).
- Postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC in #postmortems; draft report to be published to Confluence.

Attachments and references:
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C024SUPPORT/p1678684200000000
- Related PR (fix-in-progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3125
- Runbook page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/INGRESS+Thermostat+Runbook
